fixed: A test that starts the Hardcover sync worker now stops it when the test ends. Left running, the worker kept writing links and matches into the test's own temp directory after the test had returned, so the release build failed one run in several on a temp-directory cleanup error while passing locally.

On a phone whose browser keeps a bar at the bottom (Firefox on Android), the navigation bar floated one browser-chrome height above the true bottom of the screen: the shell is already sized to the visible viewport, so offsetting the bar by that same gap a second time lifted it off the edge it should sit against.

new: A stale link to the old app now lands on the new one instead of an error page: everything under /legacy/ redirects home, except the three pages that have not been ported — the spreadsheet editor, managed import and the old chat.
changes: The retired web app is gone. Its 245 modules and 19 000 lines of JavaScript existed only to draw the library screens the new app owns, and they were still being built, served and shipped in every release. What remains under /legacy/ is the three unported pages and the reader.

The app no longer installs itself as an offline shell. The service worker that used to cache the old app stays reachable only long enough to delete its caches and unregister, so browsers that still have it stop answering with pages whose files no longer exist.

fixed: The layout check that guards the phone's bottom bar finds it again: it was looking for a class name the shell stopped using when it was rewritten, so the check had been failing in every browser on every release since 0.1.90 while the bar itself was fine.
The public source tree ships its generated design-token reference again, so the check that verifies it matches design/tokens.json no longer reports drift on a file the tree never received.

new: The editor says so when a batch is larger than the server will save at once, instead of letting Review changes end in a refusal after two round trips.
fixed: Applying one book from the review panel no longer resets every other book staged for “back to the files”: that batch-wide list was sent with the single book's save.

A search, filter, collection, sort or library change clears the selection, so “Move or copy” can no longer act on books that are not on the table — with 10 selected and a search showing 2, the table also read “select all” as ticked.
While the review panel is open the table's cells are closed for editing: the panel shows a snapshot, and a cell edited behind it was written by Apply without appearing in the diff.
Writing metadata into a book's folder no longer leaves a half-written metadata.opf when the write is interrupted, and the sidecar write now reaches the disk before it replaces the old file.
A Calibre backup that was cut short by a crash no longer makes every later attempt fail with “existing Calibre backup is invalid”: it is written aside and moved into place.
The list of already-copied drop-folder files can no longer lose its marks or publish a mixture of two writers.
A library whose folder cannot be resolved to a real path now refuses to be used as a transfer source, instead of treating the server's own working directory as the library.
A batch of books can no longer load for ever when the server reports a total it will not deliver, and a new search now cancels the scan it replaced.

new: A judgement now carries a mark as well as a colour — 94% ✓, 72% ~, 31% × — so the scale still reads on an e-ink palette that has one ink, and for anyone who cannot separate two hues.
fixed: Discarding a book during review withdraws everything staged for it, including “back to what the files say”: before, a discarded book could still be the one thing Apply wrote.

The editor's keyboard now belongs to the table. It used to listen to the whole page, so Tab could not reach the toolbar and could not leave the table at all, Space selected a book instead of scrolling, and with a dialog open the keys typed into the grid behind it. Tab at the last cell is now an exit.
Tab with a cell open moves onto the next row, as Tab between cells already did, instead of stopping at the last column.
The match dialog keeps the focus inside itself, closes on Escape, and no longer scrolls the page underneath it.
Starting “Find ISBNs” while another lookup is running is no longer possible: the second job took over the progress line and left the first one running invisibly.
The single-book search returns the book's blurb again, so replacing a wrong description works instead of silently staging nothing.
Menu rows inside the editor's toolbar have their full height back — the toolbar's height rule was reaching into the popover and squashing every row to a 32px strip.
Small red text in the editor's tool panel meets the contrast minimum in every theme, and the toolbar's 32px controls are one named size rather than a number repeated in four files.

new: The metadata editor's toolbar is one row at one height and the lookup tools are chips with their explanation on hover, so the library table gets the space back.

The editor's keyboard works: the arrow keys move the cell, Tab and Shift+Tab walk the fields and wrap to the next row, Enter or F2 edits, Escape cancels, Space selects the row, Shift with the arrows selects a range, Ctrl+A selects everything, Home and End jump to the first and last column, and Page Up and Page Down move a screen of rows.

Values that are a judgement rather than a fact are colour-coded: a match percentage reads green from 90%, amber from 50% and red below, the ISBN found inside a file is green when it agrees with the book and red when it disagrees, and status badges are coloured by what they mean instead of all looking alike.

Taking a match has two modes: fill the fields a book has nothing in, or replace what the match disagrees about, including the title, authors, series, volume number, year, description and the Hardcover link.

Every candidate Hardcover returned for a book can be seen and chosen: the Match cell opens the ranked list with its scores, and the search words can be edited and searched again when the first answer is wrong.
The editor can write its metadata back beside the books as a metadata.opf that Calibre reads when a folder is imported, optionally into the EPUB itself, for libraries Mochil owns.
Each library remembers how it was last browsed (books, series or authors) and which layout, individually.
fixed: Discarding a book during review no longer brings it back in the next batch: a discarded book is set aside, the count is shown with a way to bring it back, and a whole batch can be discarded at once.
The editor's keyboard no longer stops working after the first click in the table.
Writing metadata into an EPUB no longer loses that book's match: the match follows the file it rewrote.

changes: The assistant's endpoint can be set in Settings → Assistant: the address, the model, the key and what the assistant is called, with a button that tries the connection and says what happened. Until now the only way was to edit the server's configuration file by hand.
The chat says so plainly when no endpoint is configured, with a link to that setting, instead of offering a message box that cannot answer.

Messages from the server about the assistant no longer name a particular product: it is "the assistant endpoint" whether that is a Hermes gateway or anything else that answers an OpenAI-compatible chat request.

An assistant endpoint that is not a Hermes gateway no longer reports an error. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint can answer the chat, but only a gateway keeps a list of earlier conversations; a server without one now shows an empty list instead of a failure.
The README documents the assistant properly: it is optional, it works with a Hermes gateway or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and what each of those gives you.

The assistant's replies can be read aloud. A finished answer carries a speaker button; it uses the server's narration voice when the voice runtime is installed and the device's own voice otherwise, and the button says which one it will use.

The voice chosen in the assistant settings now applies. The setting was saved but the chat never sent it, so every reply was spoken in the default voice; the choice travels with each sentence now and takes effect on the next reply.
Earlier conversations can be reopened. The assistant screen lists previous chats, opens one with its history, starts a new one and deletes one.

The assistant has a microphone and a call button. The microphone appears even when the server has no speech recognition of its own, using the browser's instead, and the call button holds a spoken conversation: it listens, sends what it heard, speaks the answer and listens again.

The new web interface is the default. It answers at the root address; the previous interface remains available under /legacy for the pages that have not moved yet. Old /next links and # links are redirected, the reader, device pairing and sign-in are unchanged, and an unknown API address answers with a JSON error instead of a page.

A metadata editor shows the library as one scrolling table: search, sort and filter across the whole library, select any number of books, and change a field, a series or an author for all of them at once. Nothing is written until the change is previewed, and every write can be undone.

Bulk metadata work runs as a job: ISBNs and Hardcover matches can be looked up across a selection or the entire library in the background, and the results are staged for review before anything is applied.

Columns can be resized, reordered and hidden, and the layout is remembered. Collections can be listed, edited and created from the table, and books can be moved or copied to another library after a dry run that reports how many would move and how many are blocked.
On a Calibre library, the fields Calibre owns (title, authors, series, series position, ISBN) are read-only and explain why instead of offering an edit that would be refused.

The AI screen's composer sits at the bottom and follows the keyboard, pictures and documents can be attached to a message, and the editor's lookup tools use the assistant configuration the server already has.
The editor's list no longer carries a match summary for books that already have a description, and it is no longer served from a cache, so an edited row comes back edited.

Smaller fixes from a measured pass over every screen: the editor's column headers were too small to click, a button sat inside a link, the way into the editor from Settings was a text link, and the composer's file input had no accessible name.

The dock no longer sits half behind the browser on Firefox. Firefox for Android keeps its own navigation bar at the bottom of the screen and lays the page out behind it, so a screen-sized frame built from 100dvh ran on underneath the browser and pushed the dock down with it. The frame now takes its height from the visual viewport, which is the only height both engines agree on, and the dock steps up by any strip the browser covers.

About now names the real build. The image used to be compiled without the version, so the panel could only say "local" - which is exactly the ambiguity it exists to remove. Versions and commit are stamped in at build time now, and the deploy command in AGENTS.md carries them.
Settings now has an About panel that names the build you are looking at: version, commit, when the server started and how long it has been up.
The same facts answer at /about in plain text, so the build can be checked from a terminal in one request without signing in.

A card now shows reading two ways only: the strip on the cover while you are part-way in, and one small green tick once the book is finished. The To read and In progress pills are gone from under the author, because a shelf where almost every card is unread was carrying a pill that said the same thing on every one.
An unfinished book that was parked or dropped still says so under the author, since the cover has no way to show that.

The shelf no longer repeats its own name and how many items it holds above the covers. The highlighted pill, or the dock, already says which shelf you are on, so the heading is now for screen readers only and the first cover sits 70px higher.
The sort control and the search, layout and AI icons now share that one 44px line.

The shelf name, its count, the sort control and the two icons are one line again. The sort dropdown had its own row under the count, which on a phone made the heading 114px tall and pushed the first cover down by 70px.
Every card carries its pill again, always one word and always the same height, so a row lines up. The cover keeps the percentage.
The text under a cover is a fixed block -- two lines of title, one of author, one pill -- so the pill sits on the same line in every card instead of drifting with the title.
Cards are flat: the artwork wash that tinted every card was reading as the page gradient coming back.
The library hub says its name once; the bar above it no longer repeats it.
A card ends where its pill ends: the spare row of height that used to sit under the badge is gone.
Every card carries the same pill height, so a row of them lines up.
A title is two lines at most: a long name clamps instead of pushing the author and the pill down the card.
The background is flat again: the gradient is gone, which is what the design has under its cards.
A card now reads title, author, then the type pill underneath them, instead of the pill floating on the author line.
The series position is a small plate on the cover corner again; the separate "Book 1" line under the title is gone, because it said the same thing twice.

Search and the grid/list switch moved up beside the shelf name, on the heading line, the way the design draws them. The bar is one row of pills again instead of pills plus a half-empty icon band, and the first cover starts about 120px higher.
The bar no longer carries a row of icons with nothing to its left; the space that band used is now the cards.

The Notes button opens a notes shelf again. It recognised one by its library id alone, so a vault saved under any other name (obsidian, journal, notes-2026) was not a note shelf: the tap did nothing, silently. The library kind decides now, and a tap with no notes shelf says so instead of leaving you looking at the same screen.

The phone header is four compact bands instead of five: the A-Z rail is gone from the shelf (the design does not show it), the pills, the name and the chips are tighter, and the first cover starts about 60px higher.
The teal gradient is stronger, so the top of the screen is visibly lighter than the bottom instead of reading as one flat colour.
The teal palette is the one on the sheets now: a nearly-black teal ground, cards a shade above it, and a cyan that glows against both, replacing the slate greys.

Bars and dividers are gone as hard lines. The screen is one continuous gradient from the top of the page to the dock, and the top bar and dock are transparent over it, so nothing cuts a seam across the background. Hairlines on lists stay, but as a hint of teal rather than a drawn line.

The chat bar says what the screen is: 'Lyana AI' with her connection state under it, then the settings and full-view icons, the way the design draws it. The library dropdown that shared that line is gone from the chat, and the conversation's own name lives in the sidebar list and the window title.
The chat page now follows the palette you chose. It was the one page that never applied the saved theme on first paint, so it stayed on the default colours while the library behind it was yours.
The card lost the ⋯ menu over its artwork: the tile already opens on tap, and the menu sat on the cover's subject. The same actions are in list layout and on the book's own page.

One badge per fact. The volume plate on the cover corner is gone (the series position is printed under the title), and the pill under the author no longer repeats the word the cover strip already says -- 'Started' over 'In progress' was one fact on two lines. What is left is what the cover cannot say: a recording ('Narrated') or 'To read'.

Grid and list are one button again, in the bar beside search, in the order the design uses: search, layout, then the activity dot. It shows the layout you are in and swapping it is a single tap; the two-button group it replaces read as two settings instead of one switch.
The grid/list switch moved up beside the shelf's name. It sat inside the chip row, so it scrolled away with the chips and read as one more destination instead of a way to change the layout.
A card is now as tall as what it says. The grid used to stretch every card in a row to the tallest one, which left a band of empty card under a one-line author -- the empty space under the titles.

The phone's shelf opens with its name and its size, the way the design sheet does: 'Library', then '6 items', then the sort control. The heading was switched off at phone width because the pill row also names the library, which left the top of the page as an unlabelled stack of chip rows.
The bar no longer repeats that name. There is one heading instead of two.

A book's reading state is back on the cover it belongs to: a short scrim at the bottom edge with '72% read' and a thin bar, as the design sheet draws it. The card body keeps the title, the author and the type pill, which say something else ('Narrated', 'To read').

Every card carries its type pill again, including the ones with progress on the cover. Only one of those two lines used to be allowed at a time, so a book you were in the middle of lost the word that told you it was narrated.

new: Matching a video library against TMDB is now a Settings job: Settings -> Libraries has one row per film or show library with its own preview-then-save action, and nothing is written until you press Save. It used to sit on the shelf as one button that could rewrite a whole wall of titles in a tap.
fixed: The blank rounded strip under the A-Z row on a phone is gone. The jump nav for audio, video and notes was hidden but still painting: the layout rule that keeps the A-Z index on one line used !important, which also defeats the hidden attribute, so a hidden nav left a 30px empty bar behind.
changes: The card's author line sits on the text baseline of the state pill beside it instead of being centred in a taller row, so it keeps closer to the title above it.
The phone bar's browse chips and A-Z index no longer paint an empty row when the app hides them, for the same reason as the strip above.
On a television, the library's poster wall is four covers across instead of six, so a cover is about a fifth of the screen instead of an eighth. Wide stills keep their own size.
Content on every TV screen keeps clear of the edge a television actually crops: five percent of the shorter side, which is 54 points at 1080p rather than the fixed 24 it used before.

new: A shelf now says what it is: its name, how many things are on it, and the order, on one line. The separate sort row is gone, so the order is stated once instead of twice.

The phone has a dock: Home, Library, Activity and Settings at the bottom, with the current place marked. The page is padded for it, so the last row of covers is never underneath it. On a wide screen it does not appear.
When something is playing, the player rests on the dock's top edge as one surface instead of two bars stacked at the bottom of a small screen.
changes: The browse chips wrap into two rows at phone width, with every label whole. They used to end at the screen edge, which read as a cut-off word rather than as a list to scroll.
A book with a series index in its title shows the clean name ('Dies the Fire') and the position on its own line ('Book 1'). A number that is the title, like 1984, is never treated as a position.
A book whose folder was named after itself no longer claims to be a series of one; the catalogue corrects that as it loads, without a rescan.
The phone's cards say where a book sits in its series ('Book 3'), under the title and above the author.
A book you opened once says 'Started' and shows no progress bar, instead of '0% read' with a one-pixel line under it. The web and the phone now use the same rule, so they cannot disagree.

Home stops asking the server for a reading list it never shows. The book continue rail was already hidden behind the media lanes, which exist only so a video or audio card can be started from Home, so deleting it removes two requests from every Home load and a toggle nobody could press. Nothing visible changes.
The dashboard's own relative-time helper is gone with it; every Home shelf already used the shared formatter.

The phone's Home no longer ends with a Finished list. Finishing a book adds nothing to Home: the library filters finished books, and a book you want back is one tap from its own menu. A Home that would otherwise be empty now says so instead of showing nothing.
The app is labelled 0.1.63 (version 16300) by the build itself, so it installs over the previous one normally.

The app carries the release's own version now. Every build since 0.1.20 called itself 0.1.20 in the file, so a phone was told it was already up to date, and Android refused to install a newer APK over an equal version number — which is why the removed Paper theme was still on your phone.
Paper is gone on the phone as well as the server once this APK is installed: a stored Paper preference moves to e-ink rather than resetting your choice.
The release build now refuses to publish an APK whose version does not match the release, and a unit test fails if the app's label ever drifts from VERSION again.

Marking a book unread no longer throws away where you were. It is a label: the book leaves Jump back in and the library says Unread, but opening it resumes at your place, and choosing Reading again clears the label.
A book that is marked unread says Unread rather than Dropped: only two statuses were being translated, so every other one fell through to the wrong word.
Manage collections tells you when the list could not be read, instead of showing an empty panel as if you had none.

Home no longer carries a folded shelf of every finished book. Finishing a book adds nothing to Home; the library filters finished books, and the Continue reading toggle still shows the most recent few with a Restore button.
Done buttons on the audio player keep saving after the position they were editing has gone, instead of failing silently.
A book that moves to another library takes its highlights and notes with it.
The podcast show list no longer replays its first page when you scroll back to it.
Books marked unread stay out of the On hold shelf, which is now only for books you parked on purpose.

A book recorded while you are scrolling the Hardcover shelf no longer appears twice. The list is kept newest-first and grows at the front, so paging by offset shifted every row down by one and repeated the last one; the panel now pages by how many rows the server has actually handed over, and drops any row it has already shown.

Home cards wear their library's badge: the kind's icon on a chip in that library's own hue, the same identity the switcher and the settings list use. The shape says what it is, the colour says which shelf it came from.

One place builds the page's security policy. The shell, the reader and the avatar page had three hand-edited copies of the same header, and the copy was the one that dropped the inline-script hash for two of them; they now share a single builder whose per-page differences are options.

The Hardcover shelf card is visible again. It is mounted hidden and the paging rewrite only ever set that attribute to true, so nobody could open the shelf at all - the strongest reason to look at a panel after rewriting it rather than only at its data.

One failing request no longer takes the shelf away or claims nothing is matched: the four lists load independently, so a transient error on one of them leaves the other three on screen and says which part failed.

A slow Hardcover lookup can no longer answer under another book. Clicking Find on a second book before the first search returned put the first book's results under the second, where Choose would have linked the wrong Hardcover book to it.
Choosing a different library or view clears a selection made on the previous one, instead of leaving a bar that says "3 selected" about books that are no longer on screen.

The matches file can no longer be written larger than the server will read back at startup. The read limit is now derived from the number of records it is allowed to keep, and a save that would overflow it drops the oldest records instead - previously the store could write a file that made the process refuse to start, taking every settings save with it.
A long search query is trimmed on a character boundary, so a pasted non-Latin title is no longer cut into invalid text that matches nothing.
The "left alone" list pages like the other three, and the inline theme script now knows about Magenta Cream, so that theme no longer paints in the default colours before the app loads.
Recording hand-linked books on Hardcover is batched into one write and throttled, instead of one Hardcover call and one full-file rewrite per book inside the request that opens the shelf.

The phone's dark themes match the browser's: Ember, Tide and Magenta Cream each moved up out of the near-black, keeping their own hue, so the same theme no longer looks like a different one depending on which screen you open it on.

The page no longer repaints itself under you. A service worker taking over fires controllerchange, and the app answered it by reloading -- so a first visit painted twice, and every new build reloaded an open tab mid-sentence. It is not reloaded now: a new version appears as "A new version is ready - Reload" and you decide when.

Ember's dark half moved one more step, to sit at the same lightness as Tide's: a warm brown at the same value looks darker than a cool slate, so the three were not actually level. Tide and Magenta Cream also moved up out of the near-black, each keeping its own hue.
The Android app wears the same values, so the phone and the browser no longer disagree about how dark a theme is.

Paper is gone. It was a light-only palette within about 3% of e-ink's light half, with the same near-black accent - the only difference was that it kept its shadows - so the picker now offers four: Ember, Tide, Magenta Cream and e-ink. A saved Paper moves to e-ink rather than resetting, on the web and the phone.

The dark themes are no longer near-black. What made them black was not the palette: a 40%-black vignette was painted over every page, so raising a palette changed nothing you could see. The vignette is a quarter now, and Ember, Tide and Magenta Cream each moved up to a mid tone that keeps the palette's hue - warm, cool, plum - while the light halves are untouched. All three stay as separate themes; the plan is one theme that suits both modes, but each is being brought up out of the black on its own first.
The editor's failure badge was rebuilt on the one danger ink rather than a fixed red of its own, which is what let it fall to 4.42:1 on the lighter surface.

The top bar no longer paints a strip of its own: it is transparent, so a page's background runs under it and the app reads as one surface. Once content scrolls beneath it, it frosts instead of turning opaque.

The dark themes moved off the near-black end. Ember, Tide and Magenta Cream each sat so close to black that the only alternative was a very bright light theme; every dark background and surface is lifted to a softer middle ground, and the light themes are untouched.

A first visit no longer loads the page twice. Installing the service worker claims the page it is running in, which fires controllerchange, and the app answered that by reloading itself - the second paint of a page the reader had just watched arrive. Only a worker replacing a live one reloads now.

The Settings → Editor page is gone. It held one switch, 'show the editor in the menu on this device'; the editor is a normal page in the menu, like Hermes, offered whenever the server says this person may use it.

The Hardcover shelf was loaded whole, which cannot work with a few thousand books: every request now asks for a page (25 rows) of one of four groups - needs a link, check these, matched, left alone - with a total from the server, and the search field is answered by the server too. Two matches at a time was all the old cap allowed once a shelf grew past 500, so the cap that silently dropped the oldest matches is now a runaway guard rather than a product limit.

Saving anything that did not change a module failed with `withdrawRestart is not defined`: the caller was added but its import was not, so the last step of every such save threw and the settings page answered 'Could not save'. The import is there, and a new test walks every module for a sibling helper it calls without binding it, so a missing import fails the suite instead of a save.

The theme no longer flashes dark for a light, paper or e-ink reader. The inline script that applies the saved palette before the first paint was blocked by the page's own Content-Security-Policy, whose hash is now computed from the bytes actually served, so editing that script cannot silently disable it again. The sign-in and first-run pages also allow the data: images they draw their field icons from; those icons were being refused by their own policy.

The Hardcover shelf no longer grows into a wall of rows. It opens with one line - how many books were sent, how many need a link, how many want checking, how many are left alone - one field that finds a book by title or author, and rows only where something is wrong. A match that looks right is a count with a 'Show them' button, a long list of unmatched books is capped until asked for, and the panel stays small with several hundred books.

The Metadata page is retired: it was inserted inside the Libraries panel, which is why its header showed above a row of library settings and 'Advanced' appeared at the bottom of it in a different width. Naming and checking new files is Import, editing existing metadata is the library editor, and the metadata providers and Hardcover shelf are now cards on the Libraries page. The scan-interval and cover-cache knobs are gone; 'Scan all libraries now' remains for the times it is wanted.

Stylesheets are no longer served stale after an update. A stylesheet requested as `file.css?v=N` is cached for a year, and eighteen of them had changed without their version being bumped, so returning visitors kept the old sheet - the settings page stayed two columns wide for weeks after it became one. Every stale version is bumped, one stylesheet now carries one version everywhere instead of a different one per page, and a new test fails when a stylesheet changes without a bump.
The narration Hugging Face token no longer travels to the browser; the settings page reports that a token is saved, and a save keeps it.
The settings document is served `no-store` like every other JSON response, and a failed save no longer answers with the server's config path.

A save that needs no restart now withdraws an earlier 'Restart now' offer instead of leaving it beside the new message, and a failed module list is reported instead of silently hiding the Hermes, Avatar and Editor pages.
Opening Settings no longer reports unsaved changes: upgrading a library's stored formats to those of its own kind is normalising data, not editing.

Saving any setting no longer fails while the environment supplies the public address. The page was shown public_url_source, sent it back with everything else, and the strict config decoder rejected the whole save with `unknown field "public_url_source"` - so changing appearance, or anything else, was impossible. Display-only fields are now dropped before the save, and a save made in that state cannot rewrite the file's own public_url to the environment's value.

A KOReader position is no longer judged against the server's clock. Pushes were compared with a timestamp this server had stamped on whatever the phone last saved, so an e-reader running even a minute behind had every push discarded in silence: the phone's older position stayed, and the e-reader later pulled that wrong place back. A push is now judged against the last push accepted, from the same clock, and is only ignored when it would change nothing at all.

Settings now show the public address this server is actually using. With MOCHIL_PUBLIC_URL set, every plugin package and pairing link already carried that address while the reading-sync panel kept echoing public_url from the config file, so a rebuild looked like it had changed nothing. The panel reports the address in force and says when the environment owns it, because editing the file would then have no effect.

KOReader plugin 1.28.0: the server address is a setting on the device. A paired plugin used to carry the address it was downloaded with, so moving the server to a domain or a new IP meant downloading and reinstalling the plugin on every device, and a download made through the public address still pointed at the LAN IP when public_url said so. Tap the Server line in the plugin menu to type a new address, or empty it to go back to the address the package came with.

Finding a phrase in a book no longer fails because of punctuation. Searching 'want to kill me?' found nothing in a book whose page reads 'He want to kill me, Julie?' -- the words are there, the question mark is not, and the search matched the text exactly. A miss is now retried once with punctuation treated as a word break; a real match is never replaced, because the retry only runs when the literal search found nothing.

Saving settings asks for a restart once, not on every save afterwards. A module switch that had been moved stayed 'changed' for the rest of the visit, so every later save claimed a module had just been switched and offered a restart again, for a change already applied.

Narration says which of its two requirements is missing. It needs the voice runtime and the module switched on, and it reported both as 'not set up' with the same paragraph about images -- so a server whose module was simply off was sent looking at its image. The panel now names the actual one.

Running the narration image is now enough to have narration. The server looks for the voice runtime where that image installs it and uses it, instead of reporting 'not set up' because nothing had written the interpreter's path into the config. An explicit setting still wins, and the model caches on the volume at /data/voice so a recreate does not download it again.

Updates no longer dead-end when the server's copy of the app build is stale. If the server offers a newer version but the file it serves is missing or older than that, the app falls back once to the published release, checks it the same way (package name, version, signing key) and installs it. Before, the only symptom was 'the update file on the server is out of date' with nowhere to go.

The narration image now starts the same server as the standard one. It had been left with the old single-folder command, so it came up with no configuration at all -- no account and no libraries, just the 'create your account' page -- on top of a data directory that was completely intact. A test now fails if the two images differ in how they start.
The narration image is published for both architectures. The job that combines them read the version from a checkout it did not have, so it failed after both images had already been pushed.

Narration now comes as a published image: ghcr.io/kevindherdt/mochil:narration carries the voice runtime, so a server chooses it by changing one line instead of building Python and PyTorch by hand. Settings -> Narration says so when the runtime is missing, rather than pointing at a document.

Adding an OPDS catalogue no longer closes the app when a source store cannot open. Each store opened the Android keystore the moment it was constructed -- during composition, for the OPDS screen -- so a locked or unreadable keystore ended the process instead of showing a message. Nothing is read until a payload is actually loaded or saved.

The release build installs the Android platform under the name it is actually published as. It is 'android-37.0', not 'android-37', so the build runner failed with 'Failed to find package' before compiling anything.
The release build uses the Android SDK already present on the build runner instead of installing another one, which failed on the runner's own tooling before the app was ever compiled.

The Android release build now signs with the project's own release key. The optimized signing configuration had the old debug key's alias and password spelled out inside it, so pointing it at a real key failed with 'keystore password was incorrect' whatever the environment said.

Mochil's Android releases are now signed by the project's own release key in continuous integration, so a new build is attached to every release automatically instead of being carried over by hand. This build is signed with that new key, so it installs over the previous one only after uninstalling once.

Library order now applies to every kind of library. A video, music or notes shelf was always listed below every book shelf however it was arranged, because the list was built from the book libraries first and the others appended. One pass in configured order now decides it.

Order in the menu collapsed to a single row that states the current order, and opens when you want to change it. Ten rows of arrows permanently open above the library cards pushed the libraries themselves off the first screen.
A library's icon in Settings wears the same colour as that library in the switcher.
The Metadata section on the Libraries page has a divider and rows of one width; the scan and cache row used to draw wider than the metadata rows with nothing separating the two.

The library switcher no longer colours every library the same. Colour came from the kind of library, so books, manga, light novels, notes and test all arrived in one amber; each library now carries its own hue derived from its id, and the icon shape still says what kind it is.

An update that cannot be installed now says why. The app used to hand whatever it downloaded straight to the Android installer, which answers 'App not installed' for a missing file, an older build and a wrong signing key alike. It now reads the downloaded package first and names the cause -- the server sent something that is not an app, it sent an older build than the one installed, or it was signed with a different key -- instead of leaving it a mystery.

Libraries can be put in the order you want in the switcher. Settings -> Libraries now opens with an 'Order in the menu' panel: drag a row, or use the arrows, and save. Home is not one of the libraries, so it stays first on its own.

The TV now looks like the theme you picked. Every palette used one fixed navy background on a television, so Ember, Tide and Magenta Cream differed only in their accent; the screen now keeps the palette's own hue, pushed down to near-black so artwork still carries the colour. Paper and e-ink, being light palettes, are pushed further so the page is not a bright wall in a dark room.

A dark accent is now actually lifted for the TV. The old code composited an opaque accent over a translucent white, which returns the accent unchanged, so Paper's near-black accent was invisible on a TV and its focused buttons looked blank.
Tide no longer shows an amber accent on a television. That override belonged to Kiln, the amber theme it replaced, and was left pointing at the palette that took its place.

Settings on a phone now uses the same card menu as the desktop: icon, name and the line explaining what the page is for, instead of a bare list of names. On a narrow screen the cards used to lose their border and their description, which left the one screen that explains each area as a list of unexplained labels.

The background glow now follows every theme, not just two of them. Magenta Cream had it on the phone but not on the web, which is why the same theme looked flatter and darker in the browser than in the app.

The server was still offering 0.1.11 as the Android download after 0.1.13 had shipped, so a phone already on the newer build was told there was nothing to install while a fresh download handed out a file newer than advertised. The advertised version now matches the app that is actually built, and a test fails the gate if the two ever drift apart again.
Ember (warm orange) and Tide (cool cyan) replace Espresso and Kiln, each with a light and a dark scheme so the phone's brightness switch applies to them too.

Reworked the two older palettes so they are actually colourful instead of two shades of the same warm mud. Espresso becomes Ember (warm near-black, genuinely vivid orange) and Kiln becomes Tide (deep teal, bright cyan); both now follow light and dark rather than pinning one brightness, so the device switch finally means something on every theme except Paper and e-ink.
A saved palette keeps working: the old ids still resolve to the family that replaced them, and the names stored by older Android builds map across too.
The sign-in page, first-run setup, TV pairing page, 404 page and both reader loading screens still showed the old BoboBooks 'B' tile instead of the Mochil mark. They now use the real app icon.
Magenta Cream now exists on Android too, matching the web theme added in 0.1.28 -- same colours, same light/dark behaviour.

New theme: Magenta Cream. Settings -> Appearance -> Theme family. Uses the mark's own colours (field #ff2e7e, pack #fff3e9, lid #8c003b) rather than a muted variant of the existing Espresso palette -- Espresso's background, accent and progress-bar hues sit close together, which reads as flat in places; Magenta Cream leans hard into contrast instead, with the accent genuinely standing apart from the background. Follows light and dark like Espresso does. Every colour pairing meets WCAG contrast (text 7:1+, accent on background 4.5:1+, text on accent 4.5:1+), matching the same bar the other themes hold.

Podcasts: subscriptions can now move in and out of Mochil via OPML, the format every podcast app already reads and writes. Settings for podcasts (Find a show -> Import or export subscriptions) can export the current subscription list as a file, or import one from another app to subscribe to everything in it at once; each feed in an import is attempted independently and reported separately, so one dead feed in a large file does not block the rest.

Settings → Hermes persona templates were all personal/romantic (girlfriend, wife, close companion) -- fine for a personal install, but the only options for someone installing Mochil fresh. Added three general-audience templates (Helpful librarian, Friendly assistant, Plain and concise) alongside the existing ones.

The Helper model fields sat inside the Hermes card with no visual signal that they are an independent connection (works without the Hermes agent at all). It now has its own divider, a "Separate from Hermes" badge and an explanatory line.

Settings → Modules could show a module as Off with "No libraries use it yet" even when it was actually running (gating itself was always correct server-side). The page recomputed on/off state from its own copy of settings.modules/settings.libraries instead of trusting the enabled field GET /api/modules already computes authoritatively -- two sources of the same fact that could drift apart. The toggle now always reflects what the server is actually enforcing.

The Import setup card (the Drop folder field) used plain unstyled browser input/button styling instead of matching the rest of the app -- a CSS specificity bug meant the app's underline-input style never applied here, and the Browse button got pushed onto its own row instead of sitting beside the field. Fixed to match every other settings form.

The folder picker's "New folder here" didn't actually say where "here" was -- confusing when it worked correctly (creates inside whatever folder you're currently browsing) but gave no visible confirmation of that. Now reads "New folder in /the/actual/path".

Settings → Hermes now explains where the Hermes address, API key and model name actually come from: turning on Hermes's own built-in API server (API_SERVER_ENABLED / API_SERVER_KEY in Hermes's .env, port 8642 by default, optionally /p/<profile> for a specific profile), with a link to Hermes's own docs. Previously the fields just sat there with no hint anyone not already running their own Hermes server would understand.

Fixed a real bug: Settings → Libraries → Advanced had its own, separate Incoming/Managed folder fields for the exact same thing the new Import page's drop-folder picker sets. Saving Settings for any unrelated reason silently wiped the drop folder Import had just set, which is why "New library…" on the Import page could fail with "managed ingest...is not available" even right after setting it up. Those duplicate fields are gone; Import owns its drop folder exclusively now.
The folder picker on the Import page was completely unstyled (missing stylesheet) — fixed, and it now matches the rest of the app.
Folder pickers everywhere can create a new folder in place, so picking a destination that doesn't exist yet no longer needs a shell.

Retired the old manual relative-path-typing "Managed ingest" workflow from Settings → Libraries → Metadata, fully superseded by the Import page. "Import preview" renamed to "Metadata path preview" to stop colliding with the unrelated new Import feature — it previews folder-structure metadata guesses for books already in a library, not file copying.

Clearer labels on the Import page: "Compare with" is now "Check for duplicates against", "Default library" is now "Copy books into", and "Managed folder (not a library)" — which read as unexplained jargon — is now "Don't sort yet — just copy them", with the explanation of what that actually means spelled out in plain language instead of a short code-y phrase.

Import now actually works. It needed a drop folder (managed_ingest.incoming_directory) that previously only existed as a config.json field to hand-edit, with no picker and no feedback beyond a message telling you to edit the configuration. The Import page now has a real folder picker for it — the managed folder it also needed is derived automatically, so picking one folder is the whole setup. The drop folder can be changed any time from the same page.

Fixed a second, deeper cause of the same symptom: the Import API itself (/api/metadata/editor/import and friends) was still gated behind the unrelated "Library editor" module even after 0.1.18 un-gated the page that calls it, so the page loaded but every request against it 404'd unless that module happened to be on.

The Storage choice (Local folder / Calibre library) in the library editor is now only shown for kinds where it actually means something — books, comics, manga, mixed. Movies, TV, anime, audiobooks, podcasts and music never offered a real choice (Calibre is a book format), so the dropdown is gone for those and the model self-heals to Local folder if it was ever saved otherwise.

Settings → Libraries now has a top-level "Import…" link to the existing import page — copy files from a drop folder straight into any writable library (Calibre libraries are correctly excluded as targets, since Mochil never writes to those). The page already existed but was hidden behind an unrelated "Library editor" module toggle that was off by default, so it was effectively undiscoverable.
Manga, comics and light novel cards on the Discover and All grids now name their series under the title, so a grid mixing several series no longer reads as an unlabeled wall of chapter numbers.

A requested server restart now replaces the running process in place instead of asking the container or systemd unit to notice it died and start a new one — a restart policy of "on-failure" never restarted it after a clean shutdown, which could leave the server down until someone started it by hand.
Movies and TV shows on Home now show their own icon instead of a book badge: the server was never telling the page what kind of library a watched item belonged to.

An upgraded server now reaches a browser that had the app open before: the offline shell is cached under a name that changes with each build, so the old page cannot be served back, and the app reloads itself once when a new version takes over.

The library switcher no longer falls back to the browser's own grey dropdown. A page served by an older shell handed the script a switcher without its wrapper, the themed menu was skipped, and the plain select showed through; it now works either way and hides the system control itself.
An updated server no longer leaves an open tab showing the app unstyled: a page asking for the previous build's stylesheet or script is answered with the current one instead of a 404.
The in-app update check finds mochil-android.apk in the data volume as well as the cache directory, so hosting the app needs nothing but the file.
The README screenshots are now taken on a demo library of public-domain titles with generated covers, built by scripts/demo-library.py.
Standard Ebooks and other EPUBs that mark one author with several roles no longer show "Unknown" as the author; the last role used to win.
The README screenshots are taken on a demo library of Standard Ebooks editions, whose text and covers are public domain.

Updating the server no longer leaves a browser showing the app unstyled until a hard refresh: a page still asking for the previous build's stylesheet or script is answered with the current one instead of a 404.
A server finds an app build in its data volume as well as its cache directory, so dropping mochil-android.apk in /data is enough for the in-app update check to work.

The app no longer asks for your server address every time you open it. A crash report used to keep it on the sign-in screen for good; it now steps aside after the first start, once you have had the report in front of you.

A server now serves an app build dropped into its data directory as mochil-android.apk, so an install that hosts the app does not need an environment variable to answer the update check. Servers that host nothing still answer plainly that no app is configured.

Choosing a palette no longer throws you out of Settings. Crossing into (or out of) e-ink rebuilt the whole screen instead of recolouring it, so the app forgot which screen was open and fell back to Home.

Signing in no longer closes the app. The podcasts screen was built by reflection through a constructor the app did not actually have, so the first signed-in screen threw "Cannot create an instance of class PodcastViewModel" and the process died.
A build-time check now fails if any screen's view model loses the constructor that reflection asks for, so this cannot come back unnoticed.
The crash report on the sign-in screen can now be shared (or selected and copied) instead of only read, so it can be sent on without retyping it.
If Mochil closes unexpectedly, the next launch stays on the sign-in screen and shows the crash report instead of resuming the screen that crashed and closing again.
Signing in no longer closes the app. The device token was encrypted on the main thread right after a successful sign-in, outside the error handling, so a Keystore failure there took the process down.

If the app does close unexpectedly, the next launch shows the crash report on the sign-in screen, where it can be copied. It used to be reachable only from Settings, which needs the sign-in that just failed.

Signing a phone in on a home server no longer fails with "temporarily unavailable". The Android login refused to run unless public_url was set in the configuration, which a fresh install does not have; it now uses the address the app itself connected to, the same way pairing already did.

new: The magenta and cream mark you picked is the app icon, the sign-in screen and the TV banner.
changes: The app can reach a server on your own network or over Tailscale. Plain http now works for private addresses; a public address still has to use https.
A Home the app could not open is fixed: the connect screen no longer refuses a perfectly good local address.

An install with no libraries opens Settings instead of looping. The server answered a browser's GET / with 303 to /#/settings, but a fragment never reaches the server, so every hop was the same request: Chrome gave up with ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS after signing in. The shell is now served and the app opens Settings itself. curl never saw it because it sends Accept: */*.
HEAD /login no longer redirects to itself (0.1.1 could not be pulled under the :0.1 tag).

HEAD /login no longer redirects to itself. A HEAD request matched neither the GET nor the POST case, fell through to the sign-in redirect and looped until the client gave up (50 redirects from `curl -I /` against an install with no account). Browsers report that as ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.

new: First public release of Mochil: your own library of books, comics, audiobooks, podcasts and video, read on a Kobo or this app, served by the Mochil container on your own machine.
The app, the server and the reading plugin are all Mochil now, in one version line.
changes: Pair the server once after installing: the app's saved settings and tokens carry the new name, so this build asks for the server again.
The app is Mochil end to end: its saved settings, decrypted credentials, session names and the update file all use the new name instead of the old one.
fixed: Nothing on the device still calls itself Mochil, so the rename does not leave a second set of keys behind. Because the names changed, this build signs the device in once more.

changes: Every shelf that wears the shared card look now takes its glow from its own artwork, not just books and series: series hubs, collections, audiobooks, podcasts and music all match.
The smallest text in the app moved half a step up (11px to 11.5, 12px to 12.5) so card metadata stops being the thing you squint at on a laptop.

fixed: The settings index painted a solid block behind its cards: the nav keeps the app shell's opaque background and a shadow of the same colour for the sticky tab bar it used to be, which showed as a black rectangle in dark mode and a white one in light mode across a page that now has a glow behind it. The index paints nothing.
changes: The settings cards have more room to breathe: 18px padding inside and 14px between them.

The settings cards are translucent now instead of solid: they take the same hairline border and lit top edge as the book and series cards, at about half the surface opacity, so the page's glow reads through them and the menu blends into the background instead of sitting on top of it.
The cards sit four across on a laptop, so all ten areas fit on one screen without scrolling.
fixed: The list-of-rows settings index is gone again — the cards were better, they only needed to stop being solid boxes.

changes: The settings index is a menu, not a wall of cards: two quiet columns of rows — icon, name, one line saying what the page holds, and a chevron — in ten rows that fit on one screen without scrolling. No boxes, no shadows; hairlines do the work.

fixed: Settings was still laid out as the old two-column shell — a 220px menu beside the panels — so the new index was squeezed into one narrow stack of cards while the panels sat a third of a page to the right, with Save floating above everything. It is one centred column now: the index fills it with three card columns on a laptop, and a page shows the way back and Save on one row, the page's own title under them, then its content.
A card's hint no longer leaves a single word alone on a second line.

changes: Cards are objects now, not tinted patches: every cover card and every Jump back in card sits a step off the page with a lit top edge, and takes a soft glow from the dominant colour of its own artwork instead of a blurred copy of it. Only cards that reach the screen are sampled, and a cover that cannot be read leaves the plain surface.
Hovering a card lifts it onto a real shadow instead of only shifting it a few pixels.

fixed: With the 'On this page' outline open, the tab strip of an open note was laid out after the article instead of above it, so the document's tab sat at the very bottom and note text ran through the 38px gap above the breadcrumb. The strip now owns the first row of the note pane and the outline layout starts one row lower.
The breadcrumb row is opaque again: text scrolling under it used to read through the breadcrumb and Publish/Edit labels.

The tab strip of an open note no longer covers the breadcrumb row: the note bar was pinning itself to the top of the pane, where the tabs drew over its top half and cut the location and Publish/Edit in two.

A note no longer loses its last lines: the note pane is a <main>, so it was taking a full-window height inside a smaller box and hanging about 20px past the bottom edge, where the workspace clipped it. The tab strip now stays visible at the top of the note at every scroll position, and the end of the text is reachable.

changes: Books wear the amber of the new warm direction instead of a blue that fought the accent; video, music and podcasts keep violet, teal and pink, and every chip is checked for 4.5:1 contrast.
fixed: A row of Jump back in cards stays level: a book with its own recording used to add a line and push its card taller than the rest.
Episode titles are readable in full — they wrap to two lines on the episode card and carry their whole text on hover.
An empty or failed shelf centres its panel in the space it has instead of hanging near the top, and its body copy is no longer the faintest grey on the page.

Jump back in is ordered by recent activity again: a reading position is stamped in milliseconds while video and audio progress is stamped in seconds, so comparing the raw numbers put every book ahead of an episode watched a minute ago.
An earlier page of the Series list that arrives after you change shelf, bucket or search is now dropped instead of prepending the old shelf's rows, which also left the next page skipping rows.

changes: Settings is now a page per area instead of eight tabs over one long scroll: the tab strip is an index of cards that says what each page is for, and opening one shows only that page with a way back. Save appears only where there are fields to save.

new: A plugin update now ends with a "Restart now" button that restarts KOReader, so the new version is actually loaded instead of needing a manual restart. Plugin 1.26.0.
fixed: The restart prompt after an update went through KOReader's Restart event handler, which silently does nothing on a device that does not install that handler — the update landed with no prompt at all.

performance: The KOReader plugin no longer holds a response of any size in memory: a status, progress or comic page reply is capped (8 MB for API answers, 24 MB for a page), so a misbehaving server cannot exhaust a reader's RAM. Plugin 1.25.0.

fixed: Scrolling back up in the Authors or Series list no longer leaves blank space: the rows the window dropped are loaded again when you reach the top, and the list keeps working after the trim.

performance: Covers no longer write to disk on every view: the file's timestamp is only refreshed once an hour, which is all the cache eviction order needs.
Jellyfin playback and progress requests no longer copy whole video and music catalogues to find one item; they compare ids and copy only the item they return.

fixed: Scrolling back up inside a long collection no longer shows blank space: the books the window dropped are fetched again as you reach the top, and the count follows the window as before.
A Jellyfin client now gets its cover art: the artwork route used to redirect into the browser sign-in, so a player holding a valid Jellyfin token was sent to a login page instead of an image.
Replacing an audio file and rescanning no longer mixes old browser-cached segments with the new one: the compatibility stream's segment URLs now carry the file's revision.
An author with more than one page of books can now reach the rest: the detail loads a page at a time and offers the remainder instead of silently stopping.
An account disabled or reset while settings were being saved could stay active in the newly published server. Account and device state is now one set per process, shared by both handler generations.
performance: Embedding metadata in an EPUB copies unchanged entries in their stored form, so a small archive can no longer make the worker decompress and recompress gigabytes.
Subtitle extraction is limited to two concurrent jobs, so repeated requests for the same video can no longer start an ffmpeg process each.

fixed: A book opened from an OPDS catalogue or a WebDAV folder now actually opens: those downloads were cached outside the folder the readers accept, so the reader closed the moment it started.
Two WebDAV files could share a cache name and the second one showed the first one's content. Names are now derived from the whole address and the file's version.
A download whose index could not be saved now reports an error instead of claiming success and then losing the book from the offline shelf after a restart.
performance: Downloading several books no longer re-reads the offline shelf four times a second: the progress line updates on its own and the shelf refreshes once when a download completes.

fixed: Closing a security hole: on an install set up through the first-run page without configured credentials, a blank sign-in was accepted as the administrator.

A password reset now also invalidates a sign-in or a reader's saved credentials that were being checked at that moment, so a reset cannot be followed by a session or device token for the old password.
A failed revocation no longer leaves an old password working from the credential cache.
Each account reads its own KoSync progress on the book sync screen; a configured KoSync username is used only by the account it belongs to.

Saving settings no longer risks losing reading progress acknowledged during the reload: the replacement server continues the same progress store instead of opening a second copy, and a reload stops if the pending progress cannot be written.
A page that fails to load no longer retries by itself forever — it waits for the Retry button, so an outage stops being a request storm.
Loading earlier books can no longer paste the previous library's books into the one on screen after you switch libraries, searches or sorts.
Two Home rails sharing one request no longer cancel each other when one of them stops loading.
Repeatedly regenerating a cover thumbnail no longer counts its size twice against the cover cache budget.
performance: Reading lists with thousands of entries no longer spend quadratic time sorting under the progress lock.
A sick podcast feed subscription reports the failure and leaves nothing half-applied in memory, so retrying actually saves it.

fixed: Switching between Covers and List inside a collection keeps the pages you have already loaded; it used to reopen at the first page and throw the rest away.

changes: Downloading a book no longer makes the shelf stutter: the progress bar updates on its own, instead of redrawing the whole library several times a second while something downloads.
A finished download still updates the shelf immediately, so Downloaded and the queue behave as before.
A collection with thousands of books opens the same way a library does: one page at a time, loading more as you scroll, instead of drawing everything at once.
"Select all" is now "Select loaded (N)" and says in its tooltip that it takes only the books loaded on screen.

Saving reading progress no longer interrupts the rest of the app: the position is kept in memory and written once every second and a half, so browsing a large library stays responsive while you read (a hard stop can lose at most that second and a half, and a normal shutdown writes everything first).
Rotating the phone keeps the film you had open instead of dropping you back to the grid.
A TV show with many seasons can be scrolled to its last season, and season 0 is called Specials, as on the phone.
Closing the reader no longer throws away the position it was sending, so another device resumes where you stopped.
Video search keeps what you type while the keyboard settles and searches when you press search, as the book and music screens already did.
Home no longer shows the pull-to-refresh spinner by itself when you come back to it.
TV posters decode their artwork once instead of twice.
The book and music search panels stay open when the phone rotates, and the music shelf is no longer blanked by a background refresh.
Sorting by author, series or date no longer disables the A–Z rail; a letter picked under those sorts filters the shelf.
Closing the search panel no longer runs the search you just dismissed, and it puts the unfiltered shelf back.
Switching between Covers and List keeps the book you were looking at on screen instead of jumping to the top.
Alphabet jumps land on the row you picked, not a row or two above it, and the first row is no longer hidden behind the top bar.
Home loads fewer bytes: the blurred backdrop no longer pulls a full-size cover, and the three shelves share one request each.
Card buttons name the book, its count and its author for screen readers; the Save to collection dialog has a name; artwork without a cover now falls back like a book cover.
The e-ink palette has visible card edges and separators (they were below 3:1 against the page).
Scrolling a long shelf reads a few card positions per frame instead of hundreds.
The sort control is a 44 px tap target on a phone, and a finished scan stops polling the server.

Server: the OPDS landing page no longer copies the whole catalogue to count it (tens of milliseconds and tens of megabytes per request), the search index rebuilds once per change instead of once per concurrent request, HTTP Basic readers stop re-hashing their password on every cover (63 ms each), the book counts file is written crash-safely, and a damaged counts or columns file is moved aside instead of stopping the server from starting.
Server: a streamed comic no longer re-sorts every archive entry for each page.

Adding a library now starts with picking its folder. Mochil recognises a Calibre library by its database, works out what is inside (books, comics, video, audio or a Markdown vault) and suggests a name, so you can check one card instead of filling in five fields.

Online metadata is no longer a per-library choice: books, comics and manga use Hardcover when its token is saved and Open Library otherwise, movies, TV and anime use TMDB, and a vault or audio library gets none. Libraries you set by hand keep their choice.

Modules has one Hardcover switch instead of three, with reading progress and ratings as options inside it. The two Hardcover/ISBN questions the Library editor can ask moved to Hermes → What she can do.
Library cards are shorter: preferred formats and folder layout sit under Advanced, while the switches that let Mochil write to your files stay visible.
Changing a library’s Content also clears an online-metadata choice that no longer fits it, so the change always saves.
The Metadata panel’s "Used by" line now names every library that will really use that provider, including libraries that let Mochil choose.
With no browsable folders configured on the server, "Add a folder…" falls back to a card whose path you can type instead of closing with nothing.
A Hardcover option that is disabled because the main switch is off no longer announces itself as on to a screen reader.
Settings → Libraries: OPDS catalogues and WebDAV libraries are now one "Add a source" entry.
Covers or List is now one setting for books, music, podcasts and video. Your existing choice carries over, and changing it anywhere changes it everywhere.

Podcast download settings are clearer: one "On this device" section (keep the newest N, Wi-Fi only) and one "On the server" section. The misleading "manual downloads" sentence is gone, and the switch rows are fully tappable.

EPUB reader: Progress bar, Chapter time left and Book time left are now one "Reading progress" choice (None, Bar or Time), in the Appearance tab with Status icons; the Display tab is gone. Your old settings carry over.
Sharper text is now simply Off or On (it was Off, Light, Medium or Strong) and starts on for e-ink devices until you choose otherwise.
Comics: manga opens right to left and other comics left to right, as on the web. A direction you set is remembered for that book.
Settings has fewer tabs: Metadata now sits under Libraries, and the Editor options sit under Modules. Remembered or bookmarked tabs open in the new place.
Removed the duplicate Reading defaults page from Settings. Text size, font, spacing, margins, pages and theme are set in the reader's own settings panel, the same saved values as before.
A book library no longer repeats the "Currently reading" strip on its Discover tab; Continue reading stays on Home.

KOReader plugin 1.24.0: the Automatic push choices are back: when closing, after changing chapter, after every page, or manual only. Pushing per page or per chapter waits two seconds after the last page turn.
Four theme families: Espresso, Kiln, Paper and e-ink. Nocturne is retired and a saved Nocturne becomes Kiln.
The comic reader's page fit is now Fit or Width. Stretch distorted pages and is gone; a saved Stretch opens as Fit.
Tap zones in the EPUB reader now start on Edges for new installs, matching the web. Anything you chose before is kept.
fixed: Removed the "Connection not checked" line from Settings, which never changed.

changes: Theme families are now four: Espresso, Kiln, Paper and e-ink. A saved Nocturne becomes Kiln.
Removed the Background picker. Espresso and Kiln keep the soft glow; Paper and e-ink stay flat.
Removed the Sign-in background setting. The sign-in screen always shows the glow, and old config files that still mention it keep loading.
Removed the duplicate tap-zone setting from Settings → Appearance. Tap zones are set in the reader, where they already were.
Hid the Book reader (Readium/Classic) setting. Readium is the default, and adding ?engine=classic to a reader address still opens the classic reader.

KOReader plugin 1.23.0: the update check always runs once a day and its switch is gone, "Test connection" lives under Plugin, and the separate Search shortcut in settings is removed. (This version also dropped the per-page and per-chapter push choices; 1.24.0 brings them back.)

fixed: Offline downloads from different libraries or servers can no longer be mixed up: two books with the same title or id no longer open each other's file. Books you already downloaded are left exactly as they are.
Removing an offline book no longer deletes a file another entry still uses, and no longer leaves a stray file behind when the entry changed in the meantime.
Books from a feed that gives no ids are told apart by their full address, so one can no longer replace another in your offline list. Such a book already downloaded is fetched again once.
EPUB reading position no longer jumps back to an older page when a slow sync finishes after you have turned pages, and a sync that failed or was interrupted is retried instead of being forgotten.
Resuming a paused audiobook or podcast queue keeps each track's length, so progress and remaining time are right after the app restarts.
Downloading several books at once no longer drops some of them from the offline list, and a damaged offline index is kept instead of being overwritten.
Streamable comics queued for download are downloaded in full.
Switching a manga or comic between Paged and Webtoon keeps your place instead of unexpectedly changing the saved page while images load.
In Paged mode, Width lets you scroll tall pages vertically, while Fit keeps the whole page visible.

changes: The book, series, series-detail and collection grids now use the screen width better on wide and mid-size screens: the same covers (about 200–250px wide) sit with tighter gaps and no wide empty margins, so 1920px fits seven columns and 1024px four. Every library kind (books, light novels, manga) uses the one rule.
Book and series titles are a little bolder in full text colour, and series titles keep room for two lines like book titles so card rows line up. Authors stay muted.

fixed: Backlinks and the vault graph no longer miss wiki links after stray or escaped backticks, invent links across code, or reject links whose display text contains brackets.
Code examples spanning multiple lines or using multiple backticks no longer appear as wiki links. Malformed notes with many nested link openers are scanned more efficiently.

A [[link]] written as an example inside a code block or inline code no longer counts as a mention: the note appeared in the linked page's backlinks and drew an edge in the graph. Code is now skipped the same way tags already skip it.
A link after an unmatched [[ is no longer swallowed: in “oops [[broken then [[Good]]” the scan resumes at the inner opener, so Good now lists the note that links to it.

KOReader plugin 1.22.0: opening a book's details no longer risks freezing the reader when the server is slow (the cover now gives up after a few seconds), and the download queue stops repainting a closed window.

A match suggested by the metadata lookup can no longer run code in the administrator's session: the publication year was written into the page as-is, and it now goes through the same escaping as the title.
Switching library or changing the search while a long list is still loading no longer leaves you looking at the previous library's rows when the slower answer arrives.

A download finishing in the background can no longer wipe out what you were doing on screen, such as a search or an open dialog: the queue used to write the whole screen state back at once from the download thread.
The library no longer keeps showing its spinner for ever if a collection is edited while the first page of books is still loading.
The app no longer does disk work on the interface thread at start-up and after every finished download, so a large downloaded library opens more smoothly.

A book added to the download queue again after it had already arrived now downloads. Before, it stayed at the end of the queue for ever while the finished copy was marked as downloading a second time, so a book you re-fetched after deleting it never landed.

new: Books can now be lined up for download. "Add to download queue" on a book's details fetches it one at a time in the order you added them, so three books for a trip can be collected while you keep browsing instead of waiting through each download. The banner at the top shows which book is arriving, how much of it has arrived and how many are still queued, and keeps showing while you move around the app. A book that fails is marked with its reason and the queue carries on with the rest.
changes: Android versionCode 416.

new: KOReader: books can be added to a download queue instead of waiting for each one to finish. The queue fetches them one at a time in the order you added them, shows how much of the current book has arrived in megabytes, lets a book that has not started yet be taken out again, and opens a finished one with a tap. A book the server refuses is marked failed and the queue carries on with the rest.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.21.0: the download path reports progress to the queue through an optional callback and a counting sink, so the plain Download button behaves exactly as before.

new: KOReader: a book that belongs to a series now offers the next volume in its dialog, by title and number, so finishing one book and starting the next no longer means going back to the library to hunt for it. The order comes from the catalogue's own series metadata, the answer is remembered per book while the dialog lives, and a book outside a series asks nothing at all.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.20.0: new device route GET /api/koreader/v1/series/<library>/<book> returning the neighbouring volumes; a book whose index is unknown is never promoted above a numbered one.

new: KOReader: the book dialog now shows the cover above the title, so you can tell two editions of the same book apart before opening either. The image is fetched once and cached beside the downloads; a book the server has no artwork for is remembered for a month instead of being asked again on every open, and any failure - no artwork, an expired pairing, a KOReader too old for the widgets - falls back to the plain text dialog.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.19.0: a cover that arrives as an HTML login page is rejected rather than cached as a broken image.

new: KOReader: Library now has an "On hold and dropped" shelf, so a book parked from the device stays reachable from the device. It lists what the web and the Android app already showed, with the status next to each title, and tapping one opens its dialog.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.18.0: the device continue route takes ?held=true, using the same parked list the other two clients read.

new: KOReader: the book dialog can set a book's status - Reading, On hold, Dropped, Read or Unread - and the dialog shows the status it currently has. On hold and dropped books leave the continue shelf and come back when you set them to Reading, so parking a book is now something you can do from the device instead of only from the web.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.17.0: setting a status is a PUT to the device's own status endpoint, so it works with the paired-device token the plugin already uses.

fixed: Continue Reading (OPDS): the feed and its navigation entry only list books that are actually being read. A book opened on page one to look at it, and one you parked as on hold or dropped, no longer appear there with "0% read" or a stale position, and the root feed no longer offers the entry at all when nothing is in progress.

KOReader: the statistics panel's "Books in progress" count now uses the same rule as the continue shelf, so it no longer counts books that were only opened or that you put aside as on hold or dropped. Pages read still counts what was read in every unfinished book.

new: KOReader: the plugin's settings are now one grouped page instead of a growing flat list - Syncing, Library, This device and Plugin, with every row showing the value it currently has (sync timing, download layout, download folder, designed home, notes and wiki, update checks), so you can read the setup without opening each entry.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.16.0: a switch flips in place and a group of choices opens inside the page, so the settings screen stays open while you change several things.
KOReader: the row that shows the server address is a label now, not something you can tap.

new: Reader: reading speed in the Stats panel - about how many pages a minute you read, next to the average time a page takes. Turn on Chapter time or Book time in the reader menu and the floating progress label also shows how long is left in this chapter and in the book.
