fixed: Reader: the time-left estimate no longer collapses when you skim. Flicking through ten pages in a few seconds used to make half a book look like four minutes of reading, because every turn was folded into a running average. The estimate is now the middle of your recent turns, and a turn far faster or slower than your usual pace, a jump to the table of contents, or a pause over two minutes is left out of it entirely.
changes: Reader: a pace that was already learnt on a device is kept after this update rather than relearnt from scratch.

new: KOReader: page bookmarks now sync. A bookmark is a page rather than a highlighted range, so it never appeared on another device or on the web; it is now uploaded and downloaded alongside highlights, and deleting one tells the other devices which page to un-bookmark.
fixed: KOReader: a deletion no longer loses what the annotation was. The tombstone used to be sent as a plain highlight with no locator, so a bookmark's page - its whole identity - was unrecoverable on the receiving device.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.15.0. Bookmarks made on any device appear on the others; an unchanged bookmark is never toggled, because toggling a bookmarked page removes it.

new: KOReader: a Reading statistics panel in the plugin menu - books in progress, books finished, finished this month and pages read across every device, plus the books finished most recently, with today's reading and this book's totals from KOReader's own statistics when that plugin is running. Answers GET /api/koreader/v1/stats.
KOReader: Search all libraries from the plugin menu, instead of only being able to search inside the list you are already looking at.
fixed: KOReader: highlights made on one reader never appeared on another. Every highlight this plugin uploads is stored under a koreader:<hash> id, and the import step dropped exactly those ids, silently and for good - the cursor then advanced past them so they were never retried.

KOReader: a highlight deleted elsewhere came back. The deletion could not be matched to a highlight made on this device (which only has a derived id), so the item stayed on screen and was then re-uploaded against the deletion's own revision, re-creating it on every device.

KOReader: highlight sync died with a Lua error on PDFs and CBZs whenever a remote id also existed locally, because the bookkeeping it reads is only created for reflowable books. No highlight, note or deletion from that book ever left the device.

KOReader: a highlight edited on two devices conflicted again on every single sync, showing the same message each time. The newer edit now wins once, against the conflicting revision, so the two sides agree afterwards.
KOReader: a download interrupted by a power cut left its staging folder behind, and that book could then never be downloaded again - every retry failed at mkdir.
changes: KOReader plugin 1.14.0. A book that is barely started now reads as <1% instead of 0%, the Continue reading row no longer describes the server's page limit, marking a book finished updates the dialog straight away, and an installed-but-not-running plugin version is described plainly.

fixed: On a Calibre-managed library the Library Editor refused a Series change but accepted the volume number beside it (the # cell, and the Renumber tool that sends one for every selected book), along with the title and author sort keys. Those fields are Calibre's own metadata, so the override was shadowed by Calibre's database - exactly what the guard exists to prevent. The guard now names the fields Calibre owns instead of reusing the list a Hardcover lookup is built from; rating, tags and publisher stay editable.

Creating a collection of picked books was two writes - the empty collection, then its members - so a failure in the second left an empty collection behind that the retry duplicated as a second one with the same name. It is now a single write.

Returning to the app no longer blanks the Video tab or a show's episode list. The progress refresh that runs on resume replaced the visible grid with a full-screen spinner - or with the error panel when the request failed - and the list came back scrolled to the top. A refresh now only takes over the screen when there is nothing on it, and a new search still shows its own loading and error state.

On a slow OPDS catalogue, a folder tap, a search or Back pressed while the first page was still loading was thrown away. Back even reported that it had handled the press, so the arrow looked dead - and with nothing on the back stack it closed the whole catalogue browser instead of leaving the folder. The newest navigation now wins, and Back records where a page load is going as it starts.

Dismissing the reader's search sheet while it was still scanning reopened it seconds later with the results of the search that had just been cancelled. A dismissed or superseded search can no longer publish its result.

On a TV Home screen that is short for its text size, the remote brought only the artwork of a Continue watching or Continue listening tile into view: the title and artist underneath stayed below the fold and the focus ring lost its room, so a focused shelf looked like a picture with no name. Focusing a tile now brings the whole tile - artwork, title, artist and the slack the ring grows into - into view.

On a TV the full description over a show or film could not be closed: the remote's arrows were still resolved against the page underneath, so the ring jumped to Play or an episode while the text was open and Close was unreachable. The description now answers every direction itself - down reads the text, the end of the text, Left or Right moves to Close, and Enter on Close puts it away.

TV Settings no longer reads as magnified. The category list, the group headings and the update changelog keep their own denser type scale instead of the ten-foot shelf scale, and the release notes sit in a bounded panel that the remote scrolls instead of pushing Check for updates off the screen.

new: On Android TV a show or anime description that does not fit can now be read in full: the description is one focus stop with a Read more label, and pressing Enter opens the whole synopsis over the page with Back returning to it. Movies get the same when their synopsis is cut off.
fixed: TV show and anime pages no longer lose the cast below the screen: title, description, Play and the seasons, the episode rail and the cast are laid out in one measured band, the way the film page already was. When a window is too short for all of it the cast steps below the first screen as one whole section instead of showing a heading with half its portraits cut off.

Episode cards on a show page are now sized from the window they are drawn in: a taller screen gets bigger episode stills, and a short one keeps a whole card on screen instead of a cropped row. The description keeps its line count when you move along the rail, so the episode row no longer jumps as each episode's synopsis loads.

A rescan now publishes metadata that changed only in a sidecar file: tags, publisher, rating, identifiers, title sort and read-along were left out of the comparison, so a Calibre tag or rating edit showed nothing until the server restarted.
Taking back a library transfer restores only the corrections it moved, instead of the whole override store, so corrections made in between are no longer discarded.
A disabled account's KOReader device token now stops working. Chat ownership in the Hermes screen no longer comes from a string prefix, so one account can no longer open another's conversations.

Pausing a movie or audio conversion no longer leaves the session stuck: a queued job cancelled before it started used to make every later attempt answer "still stopping", and its source file was never closed.
Book files are now flushed to disk before the library move unlinks the original, and an interrupted cross-device move finishes instead of being refused for ever.
Hardcover now receives the last pages of a session; the throttled progress it held back was never sent because the same rule was applied twice.
Read-aloud now produces sentences for Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai and Cyrillic books instead of an empty chapter, and a replaced EPUB no longer plays the previous recording's audio.
Opening a publication from the cache no longer re-sends the whole file on every open, and album downloads now fail visibly instead of delivering a truncated archive.

Smaller fixes: epub series-index and title repair, ComicInfo.xml handling, ISBN-10 check digits, the import screen's filter selection, the theme flash on first paint, the Continue reading page length, and the Android device diagnostics upload.

On Android TV the navigation panel no longer opens by itself when a movie's page opens or when you go back to the shelf. Opening a film now puts focus on its Play or Resume button, and going back returns to the poster you left.

A note saved as .markdown is now editable in the wiki editor, like a .md note. It used to open read-only and refuse edits, and its text was not read byte-for-byte, so the editor could not tell a real conflict from its own normalisation.

The same notes now appear in the offline notes bundle KOReader downloads and can be polished like any other note; both checks asked for exactly "md" while the rest of the app has treated both extensions as Markdown for a while.
There is one definition of "is this Markdown" now — the catalogue's own extension table — so a read, a write and a bundle cannot disagree about it again.

A KOReader catalog page opened with an offset past the end of the list (a stale resume point, or a hand-edited link) could crash the request instead of showing an empty page: the paging math added the offset and the limit before clamping them, so a very large offset overflowed to a negative number and the slice panicked. The collections list and the TMDB matching run now share one overflow-proof window helper with the rest of the KOReader paging.

A read-along book whose chapter or narration file name contains a "#" played no narration for that chapter: the overlay unescaped the href before splitting off the fragment, so "track%232.mp3" was looked up as "track", every clip in the chapter was dropped, and the chapter href no longer matched the reading order. Build, the overlay and the text-only download now share one resolver.

Notes saved as .markdown were missing from the link graph: the graph filtered pages on the bare "md" extension while the rest of the store treats .markdown as Markdown, so those notes never appeared as nodes and their [[links]] produced no edges.

TV show and movie details now measure the actual title, actions, synopsis and episode cards inside the available screen, including the playback dock, instead of estimating their heights. This fixes reproduced title clipping on constrained screens and after returning from Cast.
The Cast heading and portraits are kept together: the complete section is visible when it fits, or starts below the fold and is revealed with the remote.

Movie Play/Resume and watched controls have smaller visuals while retaining 48dp remote targets. Home uses a smaller heading and landscape Continue watching cards to leave more room for the next section.

A highlighted episode card grows slightly and wears a halo, and that growth was not part of the space the page reserved - so the page still shifted by a few millimetres and clipped the title. It is counted now, at every text size.
The synopsis is a step smaller, the Play/Resume and season buttons are smaller, and the cast row sits lower, which gives the episodes the room they need without pushing the title off the top.
The movie page follows the same rules: its title and its Play/Mark watched buttons stay inside the screen instead of relying on a scroll nobody asked for.

A show's title is no longer cut off at the top once you start browsing episodes: the page now measures the window and the text size it is actually running at, and shortens the episode synopsis - or gives up the year line - rather than scrolling the title out of sight.

The movie page had the same dead space and the same problem: the cast row could spill past the bottom edge with no way to reach it. It scrolls now, and both pages put the cast row clearly below the episode cards.

Browsing episodes no longer scrolls the show's title, year line and synopsis off the top of the screen: the page kept 96dp of empty space at the bottom for a bar that is not there, which is what forced the scroll. The header and the episode rail now fit, so they stay put.
The cast row sits below the fold instead of crowding the episode cards, and stepping back up into the episodes puts the page back exactly where it was.

A show's page showed two long synopses at once - the show's on the left and the focused episode's on the right - so they read as one paragraph printed twice, and the right-hand one ran off the screen. There is now one synopsis, in one place: focusing an episode swaps it for that episode's.
Wide list rows - an episode in Continue watching, a season's entries - no longer cut off their own titles: the row grows with its text instead of clipping at a fixed height.
The screen stopped wobbling while moving around, because the text that used to appear and disappear beside the rail was changing the row's height.

On a short window, or with large text, the story now takes two lines instead of three so the episode rail still fits above the bottom bar, and stepping back up from the cast row returns the page to the story instead of leaving it scrolled out of sight.

changes: TV posters now carry a hairline edge. The tile fill sits barely above the page colour, so without it a shelf read as captions floating on black rather than as objects.

Covers and tiles now carry a hairline edge and lift slightly on hover instead of relying on their fill, so a shelf reads as objects rather than captions floating on the page. On e-ink the edge is drawn in the text colour, and the hover lift is a plain brightness step rather than a shadow.

Themes are now Mochil' own instead of named after operating systems: Espresso (default, with a warm light twin), Kiln, Nocturne, Paper and the e-ink device palette. Kiln, Nocturne and Paper look the same in light and dark mode because they define one look; Espresso keeps a daytime twin for anyone who wants the device switch to matter.

A theme saved by an older version is not lost: it wears the nearest of the five (Dusk, Twilight, Tide, Manjaro and Material become Kiln; Ember, Rosewood and Ubuntu become Espresso) instead of falling back to a blank look.

The app now ships Mochil' own themes instead of ones named after operating systems: Espresso (the default, warm and dark, with a warm light twin for daytime), Kiln (a mid-tone that looks the same in any device mode), Nocturne (cool ink with violet) and Paper (flat and high contrast). E-ink keeps its own device palette.

new: Each area of the app now carries its own accent colour inside whichever theme you picked: video leans violet, music teal, podcasts rose and comics gold, while books keep the theme's own accent. Every value was contrast-checked against its theme's surface, and the e-ink theme keeps everything at the text colour.

fixed: The TV backdrop no longer washes the screen in Material's default pink: every palette now contributes its own tint, so the glow behind the artwork belongs to the theme you picked.
Keyboard focus on TV is easier to find from the sofa: the focus ring gained a soft halo so it stays visible against busy artwork.

changes: The TV app has a type scale built for a sofa rather than a phone: synopsis text and captions are noticeably larger and the title-to-body steps are a real ramp, so nothing on screen is unreadable from three metres. The list rows grew to match.

fixed: Moving books between libraries can no longer leave a half-finished transfer that reports success: the move is written down before anything changes, every step is recorded as it lands, and a step that fails answers with which step stopped instead of claiming the whole thing worked.

An interrupted transfer finishes itself: the recorded move is replayed at startup and with the ten-minute rescan, so reading positions, metadata and custom columns end up with the books that moved rather than staying behind in the old library.
The note bar's alignment is limited to the reading view: opening a note for editing brings its formatting toolbar back to full width instead of squeezing fourteen buttons into a 148px strip.

Closing your player no longer stops the stream somebody else is watching: one encoder serves everyone viewing the same episode, so a stop request now only cancels it when no other account has fetched it in the last half minute.

A Word document saved as RTF opens in the web reader even when it contains a picture: the size check now measures the text it produces instead of the uncompressed file, so a two-line note with an embedded photo is no longer refused or left out of search.

A book with thousands of large chapters can no longer make the reader spend gigabytes of memory: letting a scroll through image-only pages stops after a fixed amount of probing, so the pages it does not reach simply read normally.
One unreadable or just-deleted file no longer empties the whole note library: the scan skips it and keeps the pages it did read, instead of failing the refresh that followed a save.
A page saved as .markdown now appears in the backlinks of the pages it links to, like .md notes already did.
Switching the graph from everything to a single page no longer freezes it on the old picture or throws when the pointer is still over a node.
Opening a tag while a note is loading no longer replaces the note you just opened, and a tag list that fails says so instead of doing nothing.
On a phone, opening a note now closes the sidebar properly, so the menu button stops announcing the wrong state and the drawer no longer springs open again on the next refresh.
A season that failed to load can be reopened instead of staying broken until the page is reloaded.
Finding a book's reading position on a KOReader device can no longer offer a position from a different book, and the offer is looked up for the signed-in reader.
Editing a book's identifiers now counts as an ISBN change, so Calibre-owned ISBNs are refused like the rest of Calibre's metadata and cached matches are re-queried.

A KOReader position that arrives while the book index is finishing no longer waits a full minute to appear in the reader: the pass that missed it asks for another pass straight away, and an update that genuinely belongs to a different copy of a book is still retried only when the library changes.

A note's backlink list no longer comes back a version behind: when another note is indexed while the list is being rebuilt, the rebuild now repeats instead of answering from the previous index and hiding the newly linked notes.

A reading position saved twice in the same second, or while the server clock stepped backwards, is now kept: the newest save always wins instead of being dropped behind a success reply while the device believed it had synced.

Text inside a Word text box is no longer doubled when a document's text is extracted: Word stores the same text twice, once for modern renderers and once for legacy ones, and only the first copy is read now.

changes: The bar above a note now lines up with the note: the breadcrumb sits over the title it names and the actions end where the text ends, instead of drifting to the window edges. On a narrow window the same bar keeps a small margin at the edge.

fixed: A chapter whose file name contains a hash - stored percent-encoded in the EPUB package file - no longer disappears from the reading order.
Progress from a book that was deleted or moved stops matching its old content hash, so KOReader progress goes to the book that is actually there instead of a leftover entry.

Previews near the end of a video still render: the keyframe-only decode is used only where a keyframe can follow the seek, and the last buckets keep the slower full decode so scrubbing to the very end does not lose its preview.

performance: Video timeline previews generate about three times faster: a first preview took 2.4s on a 1080p episode and now takes about 0.8s, so scrubbing a timeline no longer stalls.
Previews decode only the keyframe at the requested position and skip audio and subtitle streams, instead of buffering a hundred frames to choose one.

fixed: On TV, the focused cover's title and metadata now show in the header. Every grid already reported them, but the header never read them, so a viewer only saw a truncated caption under each cover.
The TV grid no longer reserves 130dp of empty space at the bottom; the shell already makes room for the playback dock only while it is visible, so a shelf shows a full second row again.
TV screens keep a shared 24dp clear margin from the panel edge, so the navigation rail, dock and content survive a TV that overscans.
The TV backdrop dissolves instantly when reduced motion is on, instead of restarting a 400ms full-screen crossfade on every D-pad step.

The play button in the music playback bar now sits on the bar's centre line. Its close button used to be the sixth control in the transport group, which pushed play 21px left of centre and made the bar look off.

Library kind icons are readable on light themes: each kind now has a darker twin used when the surface behind it is light, instead of a pastel that measured about 1.2:1 against a near-white background.
The phone header now shows the library name next to its icon, so two libraries of the same kind no longer look identical.
An album or audiobook header keeps its title: play, shuffle and the action menu moved to a second row, so the name is no longer ellipsized away on a 320-360dp phone.
Music and audiobooks explain an empty Discover shelf instead of showing blank space.
The music and audiobook sorting panel now opens inside the window: it aligns to its button instead of running 79px past the right edge on a desktop width.
RTF documents are read in the code page they declare, so Cyrillic and other non-Western text no longer comes out as Windows-1252 mojibake.
RTF binary picture payloads are skipped instead of being parsed as document structure, so a readable document no longer fails to open because it contains an image.
KOReader progress waiting for a book to be indexed is queued per reader, so two people syncing the same document both reach the dashboard.
The Library Editor forgets a cached Hardcover lookup when a title, author, series or ISBN changes, so a corrected book is looked up again instead of reusing the old candidate.
changes: The Library Editor no longer writes metadata that Calibre owns. Title, authors, series, ISBN and whole-book resets are refused for a Calibre library with an explanation, while other fields and libraries are unchanged.

fixed: An EPUB table-of-contents label keeps text that follows inline markup, so "Chapter One continued" is no longer shortened to "Chapter One".
Table-of-contents links that point inside the navigation document itself (#section) are kept instead of vanishing from the list.
RTF text keeps emoji and other supplementary characters instead of replacing each half of them with a replacement glyph.
Notes refuse to save a state file larger than the store can read back, so a restart no longer opens an empty notes store after a large save.
Undoing a Library Editor batch keeps its token when the undo fails, so retrying works instead of reporting the change as no longer undoable.
Vault tags no longer drop .markdown notes; every Markdown extension is indexed.
A code fence is closed only by its own marker, so a ~~~ line inside a backtick block cannot hide later tags.
ODT text:s keeps its declared space count instead of collapsing to one space.
RTF em dashes, en dashes, bullets and curly quotes are converted instead of dropped.
Document search snippets keep the matched word when lower-casing changes the text's byte length.
performance: An image-only chapter that appears twice in a spine is split once, and generated pages are capped per archive.
changes: Images inside an HTML comment no longer become phantom pages in image-only EPUBs.

fixed: Opening a show now always moves its hero to the top of the grid, instead of leaving it in its original position beside or below closed cards

changes: Episode preview cards no longer show a 'Preview description' button; the description is revealed inline by selecting the card
The expand/collapse control is a compact icon shown only when the episode description overflows its box

fixed: Episode previews stay stable while browsing and can be expanded for the full description
changes: Select an episode card to play directly without a separate Play button under each card
Phone video show details feature a poster-led header and readable episode rows; Continue Watching remains on Home instead of repeating in video libraries
Video episodes use clearer descriptions and mobile-friendly rows with separate preview and play actions

fixed: Replaying a finished video starts at the beginning and saves the new position without overwriting newer playback progress
Selecting a finished episode starts it from the beginning instead of potentially skipping straight to the next episode
TV show descriptions retain a stable height when navigating episodes, and cast focus outlines fit their portraits

changes: TV show details place episodes above cast and use more compact Play, Next and season controls

new: TV and mobile: matched movies and shows can display TMDB cast portraits, names and roles, with a fallback when no portrait is available
Mobile movies open a details screen with a synopsis, cast and playback controls
Video libraries can show cast portraits and roles for matched movies and shows, and episode synopses when available

changes: Library settings clarify that opening matched video titles can fetch TMDB details, cast and episode information

new: TV: show and movie details can display cast from a matched TMDB title, and focusing an episode shows its description when available
changes: TV movie details now place the poster alongside a larger title, synopsis and playback controls on wide screens

fixed: Music and audiobook streaming (compatibility mode): seeking far ahead in a long track could fail with "Compatibility stream is not ready" after a 20 second wait, because the server never started preparing the part of the track you jumped to; it now starts encoding at the point you seek to, so long tracks, audiobooks and podcast episodes can be scrubbed to any position

Video streaming cache: when two transcodes finished at the same moment, the cache size counter could be reduced twice for the same cleaned-up session, so it under-counted real disk use and the cache could grow past its size limit before old sessions were cleaned up

Managed ingest discovery: paging through a source folder could silently skip a file whose name sorts just before a sibling folder's contents (for example "Album!.mp3" next to an "Album" folder), so it never appeared on any page; the listing is now ordered the same way the page cursor compares names

PDF/comic reader: the saved page position is now written atomically (temp file + rename, fsync'd before replacing the previous version) instead of via SharedPreferences.commit(), so an app kill, crash, or power loss mid-save can no longer leave a truncated progress file that broke all further saves for that reader; a corrupt or missing file now just reopens at the start of the book

TV: the subtitle-appearance text-size and background-opacity sliders, the library search box, and the TV pairing screen's server-address field now show the same focus ring every other TV control uses, instead of Material's faint default outline at 10-foot viewing distance

fixed: Podcasts/Music: resolving a downloaded track's offline playback URL (a disk/Binder-backed check) no longer runs on the UI thread when playing, queuing next, or adding to the queue; local-device and WebDAV playback (which need no such lookup) are unaffected

A rapid double-tap on play/play-next/add-to-queue could, after the above fix made that work asynchronous, apply out of the order it was triggered; queue-mutating actions on the same player now serialize in call order
Podcasts: the device download-policy dialog's settings were re-read from disk on every unrelated recomposition of the podcast screen while the dialog was open, instead of once when it opened

Podcasts: downloaded-episode lookup (a disk/Binder-backed check) no longer runs on the UI thread when opening Podcasts, toggling a download, or after an automatic download finishes; it is fetched off-thread and the screen updates once it resolves

Read-along/narration: backing out of a book while its playback service was still connecting could, once the connection completed late, revive a released player and (for read-along) restart its repeating position-tracking loop forever, leaking the connection and the reader screen behind it

performance: Bulk-import review step no longer re-scans the whole list of server-confirmed-ready files for every chosen row (twice); a one-time lookup set keeps this linear even for a batch of thousands of files

fixed: bookstats/bookcheck/filefacts stores: Save() released its lock before writing to disk, so two concurrent saves (e.g. counting/quality-check/ISBN jobs for two different libraries) could finish their writes out of order and silently revert the persisted file to older data, even though the newer data was still correct in memory

Music 'File names' button: its DOM-mutation watcher was scoped to the whole document and ran forever after the first visit to the music view, re-scanning on every unrelated app-wide DOM change for the rest of the session; now scoped to the music view's own item container
